study type: Retrospective Cohort Study with Trend Analysis
cohort: The study analyzed 813,921 obstetric inpatient delivery events in Scotland between April 1998 and March 2013, focusing on pregnancies to mothers with type 1 (n=3229) and type 2 (n=1452) diabetes compared to those without diabetes.
finding: Despite increased interventions like earlier delivery and higher Caesarean section rates in women with diabetes, higher birthweights were recorded, and improvements in stillbirth and perinatal mortality seen in the general population were not reflected in the diabetic population.
mod_finding: Both elective and emergency Caesarean section rates were greatly increased in women with diabetes compared to those without, and generally increased over the 15-year study period.
birth_weight: Gestational age-, sex- and parity-adjusted z-scores for birthweight were higher in offspring of mothers with type 1 diabetes (1.33 ± 1.34) and type 2 diabetes (0.94 ± 1.34) compared to the non-diabetic population.
gest_age: Delivery occurred 2.6 weeks earlier in type 1 diabetes (36.7 ± 2.3 weeks) and 2 weeks earlier in type 2 diabetes (37.3 ± 2.4 weeks) compared to women without diabetes, with markedly increased proportions of preterm delivery.
